sn41.2:2.2: The term of address “Honorable Senior” (_bhante thera_) is found only in this sutta and the next two. Note that when _bhante therā_ is used above, the plural _therā_ is nominative, whereas here the singular is vocative.
sn41.2:2.3: This question is also asked at [sn35.129:1.4]().
sn41.2:2.4: The expression “senior venerable” (_āyasmā thero_), found in this sutta and the next, is rare, and in early Pali invariably associated with some failing of the senior monastics. In [sn21.10]() a “Venerable Senior” is suggested to be senior in name only, while in [sn22.90]() the advice of the senior venerables is ineffectual. Perhaps the piling up of excessive titles was felt to be a sign of pomposity.
sn41.2:3.1: Isidatta’s verse is at [thag1.120](). This is not the chamberlain Isidatta of Māgadha ([sn55.6:1.4]()).
